| SRC-BNK-007 | news | Reuters / Bloomberg — PETRONAS Aramco exit from Pengerang; PETRONAS full takeover |  |
| SRC-BNK-008 | analysis | Pengerang Integrated Complex cost overrun — US$16B original → US$27B actual (69% overrun) |  |
| SRC-BNK-009 | news | Bloomberg / Reuters / Straits Times — PETRONAS Group retrenchment ~5,000 workers (10% workforce), June 2025 |  |
| SRC-BNK-010 | analysis | EIA / MOF Malaysia — Malaysia crude production ~571-604K bpd; net importer status |  |

---

"Kalau bapa settle — dia settle senyap. Kalau bapa cerita — dia bayar masa. Tapi bapa yang tahu tapi still tak settle — itu bapa yang pilih siapa yang kena bayar."

MALAM 16 September 2026. Hari Malaysia. Anwar Ibrahim berdiri di Kuching — ibu negeri Sarawak — dan cakap depan seluruh negara:

"There is no reason why this cannot be resolved."

Makcik dengar sekali. Dua kali. Tiga kali. Lepas tu Makcik tanya satu soalan je:

Kalau takde sebab tak boleh selesaikan — kenapa belum selesaikan?

## DULU — KONTEKS UNTUK PEMBACA BARU

Makcik explain sikit untuk readers yang baru masuk.

Malaysia ada dua syarikat minyak yang tengah gaduh. PETRONAS — syarikat minyak negara, 100% milik kerajaan persekutuan melalui MoF Inc., nilai hampir RM600 bilion (anggaran penulis — tiada market cap PETRONAS public; angka dari perbandingan Pengerang + downstream valuation). Petros — syarikat minyak Sarawak, ditubuh 8 Disember 2017, sebab Sarawak kata "minyak ini atas tanah kami, kenapa kami dapat sikit sangat?"

Selama ini, PETRONAS bayar Sarawak 5% royalti untuk minyak dan gas yang keluar dari tanah Sarawak. 5%. Sarawak kata tak cukup. Sarawak minta naik sehingga 20% (undi Dewan Undangan Negeri 2024). PETRONAS kata tak boleh sebab PDA 1974 letakkan kawalan petroleum di tangan persekutuan.

Siapa yang buat undang-undang tu? Kerajaan federal masa darurat 1974. Siapa yang tak ditanya? Sarawak.

Sarawak sabar 52 tahun. Lepas tu Sarawak buat syarikat sendiri — Petros — dan kata: "Kami buat sendiri lah. Gas kami, tanah kami, kami yang jaga."

PETRONAS? Fail ke Mahkamah Persekutuan pada 12 Januari 2026. Sarawak? Counter-fail cabar constitutionaliti PDA 1974. Dua-dua dalam mahkamah sekarang. Dan Perdana Menteri — yang pegang dua jawatan serentak, PM DAN Menteri Kewangan — cakap malam tadi: "takde masalah yang tak boleh selesaikan."

Makcik tanya lagi: kalau betul takde masalah — kenapa mahkamah penuh?

## BERAPA KALI SUDAH?

- Januari 2026 — PETRONAS fail di Mahkamah Persekutuan.

- Februari 2026 — pendengaran penuh counter-claim Sarawak cabar constitutionaliti PDA 1974 (fail asal difailkan lebih awal; panel 5-hakim luluskan justisiability Julai 2025).

- Jun 2026 — Anwar antara Jun-September 2026 beberapa kali cakap "hampir settle" / "akan difinalise" — petikan spesifik tidak dapat disahkan pada waktu publikasi.

- September 2026 — kunjungan Hari Malaysia ke Kuching dengan pengumuman geran khas RM1.5 bilion.

Makcik kira: sekurang-kurangnya tiga kali dalam 9 bulan Anwar kata nak settle. Tiga kali masih belum settle. Kalau Makcik cakap nak bayar bil tiga kali dalam 9 bulan tapi tak bayar lagi — bilik air makcik kena potong air.

Tapi masa yang sama? PETRONAS dividend 2024 jatuh kepada RM32 bilion — turun daripada RM50 bilion pada 2022 (rekod tertinggi) atau RM40 bilion pada 2023, sebab profit group jatuh 15% kepada RM19.2 bilion dan revenue turun 7% kepada RM320 bilion. Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC/Refinery & Petrochemical) yang menelan kos US$27 bilion (~RM127 bilion) — 69% lebih dari bajet asal US$16 bilion — sebab Saudi Aramco keluar dari projek tu dan PETRONAS ambil alih penuh. Segmen downstream PETRONAS rugi bersih RM15.2 bilion pada 2024, sebahagian besarnya dari Pengerang. PETRONAS Group umumkan perampingan ~10% workforce (~5,000 pekerja) pada Jun 2025, hiring freeze sampai Disember 2026 — bukan khusus PRefChem. Pengeluaran minyak mentah Malaysia 2024 jatuh 3.5% kepada ~181.6 juta tong; Malaysia dah jadi negara pengimport bersih minyak mentah sebab penggunaan domestik (~700,000 tong/hari) melebihi pengeluaran (~571,000-604,000 tong/hari). CEO PETRONAS Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik lanjutan kontrak sekurang-kurangnya tiga kali: Julai 2023, 2025, dan Ogos 2026.

Siapa yang potong air siapa ni sebenarnya?

## RM1.5 BILION — HARGA TIDAK SETTLE

Dalam hari yang sama Anwar cakap "bekerja sebagai pasukan," kerajaan persekutuan umumkan RM1.5 bilion geran khas kepada Sarawak (Sabah juga terima jumlah sama). Duit rakyat. Duit cukai. Duit yang sama yang patut bayar sekolah, hospital, jalan raya.

Makcik tanya: untuk apa?

- Untuk settle dispute? Belum settle.

- Untuk formula royalti baru? Belum ada formula.

- Untuk agreement komersial? Belum sign.

Jadi RM1.5B tu bukan penyelesaian. RM1.5B tu bayaran sewa status quo. Bayar supaya Sarawak tak tarik sokongan. Bayar supaya kerajaan tak jatuh. Bayar supaya Anwar boleh duduk kerusi dia lagi.

Sama macam Makcik bayar jiran sebelah RM1.5B supaya jiran tak cakap pasal tanah yang Makcik dah ambil 52 tahun. Lepas tu Makcik kata "kita kena bekerja sebagai pasukan."

## KUCHING BUKAN VENUE. KUCHING IALAH BAYARAN.

Anwar pergi Kuching. Cakap depan Sarawak. "Takde masalah yang tak boleh selesaikan."

Tapi hang fikir — kalau bapa nak settle dengan anak, dia settle dekat mana?

- Dia settle senyap. Satu surat. Satu signature. Tak payah pergi Kuching. Tak payah ceramah.

- Tapi Anwar pilih sidang media. Dia pilih Kuching. Dia pilih Hari Malaysia.

Sebab nak settle tak cukup. Dia nak orang NAMPAK dia settle.

Bila bapa beritahu seluruh kampung dia nak settle dengan anak — maknanya belum settle.

Bila bapa settle betul-betul — kampung baru tahu lepas selesai.

Orang yang betul-betul settle, settle dulu — cerita lepas. Bukan cerita dulu, harap orang ingat cerita sebagai penyelesaian.

## "TAKDE MASALAH YANG TAK BOLEH DISELESAIKAN" — BETUL KE?

Makcik tanya readers semua — betul ke?

Undang-undang yang govern minyak Malaysia (PDA 1974) dibuat masa darurat. Parlimen tak berfungsi normal. Sarawak tak ditanya. Tiada siapa konsultasi dengan negeri yang punya minyak tu.

Selama 52 tahun, Sarawak dapat 5%. Siapa yang audit tak pernah adil? Tiada siapa.

Sekarang dua-dua pihak dalam mahkamah. Kedua-dua tengah tunggu hakim putuskan.

Dan Anwar cakap "takde masalah yang tak boleh selesaikan."

Makcik tahu satu benda yang tak boleh selesaikan: masalah yang tak boleh diakui.

Anwar tak pernah akui PDA 1974 dibuat masa darurat. Dia tak pernah akui royalti 5% tu tak adil. Dia tak pernah akui PETRONAS ialah syarikat yang federal pegang — bukan kerajaan Sarawak punya.

Kalau kau tak boleh cakap masalah tu ialah apa — kau tak boleh cakap masalah tu boleh selesaikan.

## BANG NON JENIS TAKDE TELUR?

Makcik bukan nak panggil dia pengecut. Pengecut tak berani pergi Kuching.

Makcik panggil dia Bang Non jenis takde telur sebab lain:

- Dia berani pergi tapi tak berani settle

- Dia berani cakap tapi tak berani sign

- Dia berani bayar RM1.5B tapi tak berani audit PDA 1974

- Dia berani kata "finalise" tapi tak berani tanya siapa yang kena sign

Bang Non ada keberanian untuk keluar rumah. Tapi tak ada keberanian untuk tutup pintu.

Dan ini — ini yang buat dia bukan pengecut biasa. Pengecut biasa lari. Bang Non berani keluar rumah, berani cakap depan kampung, berani bayar duit — tapi tak berani buat benda yang paling penting: decide.

## APA YANG MAKCIK TAK NAMPAK DULU — SHADOW BANG NON

Makcik kena tahu satu benda.

Anwar Ibrahim ialah PM DAN Menteri Kewangan serentak. Dua jawatan dalam satu orang. Dan PETRONAS? 100% milik kerajaan — milik Menteri Kewangan. Maknanya: Anwar ialah pemilik PETRONAS. Bukan chairman. Bukan CEO. Pemilik.

Jadi bila dia kata "aku akan bincang dengan PETRONAS" — dia bercakap dengan syarikat dia sendiri. Sama macam bapa bincang dengan cermin. "Nak tanya sikit pasal rumah kita."

Tapi yang lebih penting: Siapa yang pegang majoriti kerajaan sekarang? GPS dari Sarawak. Parti Sarawak yang sokong Anwar jadi PM. Kalau GPS tarik sokongan — kerajaan jatuh.

Anwar stuck. Tak boleh bagi terlalu banyak pada Sarawak — UMNO kata "kau jual kedaulatan." Tak boleh tolak Sarawak — GPS cabut, kerajaan jatuh. Tak boleh serah kepada mahkamah — lambat, Petros terus grow.

Dan dia TAHU semua ni. Dia tahu sejak mula.

Dan DIA STILL PILIH UNTUK TAK SETTLE.

## KENAPA? — SEBAB DIA DAH DECIDE SIAPA YANG KENA BAYAR

Inilah shadow paling gelap PMX.

Anwar bukan tak tahu. Bukan tak mampu. Bukan tak berani pergi Kuching.

Dia tahu, dia mampu, dia berani pergi Kuching — dan dia STILL pilih untuk tak settle.

Kenapa? Sebab settle bermakna dia kena jadi villain.

- Kalau Anwar bagi Sarawak lebih royalti — UMNO kata "kau jual kedaulatan negara"

- Kalau Anwar tolak tuntutan Sarawak — GPS cabut sokongan, kerajaan jatuh

- Kalau Anwar serah kepada mahkamah — lambat bertahun-tahun, Petros terus grow, terus kuat

- Kalau Anwar akui PDA 1974 tak valid — seluruh petroleum regime Malaysia runtuh

Semua jalan = Anwar jadi villain.

Jadi dia pilih jalan kelima: bayar RM1.5B, cakap "bekerja sebagai pasukan," pergi Kuching, pilih Hari Malaysia, buat sidang media.

Bukan sebab dia settle. Tapi sebab dia nak orang INGAT dia settle — walaupun dia belum settle.

Dan siapa yang kena bayar kos setiap tahun yang berlalu tanpa penyelesaian?

Rakyat.

Sebab tiap tahun tanpa agreement: gas import mahal, subsidi terbakar, harga naik, duit sekolah kurang, duit hospital kurang. Bukan Anwar yang bayar. Kita yang bayar.

Anwar tak settle sebab dia protect Anwar. Bukan sebab dia protect Malaysia.

## APA MAKCIK NAMPAK SEKARANG:

- Bila PM pegang dua jawatan — PM + Menteri Kewangan — dan PETRONAS ialah anak syarikat MoF Inc — dia bercakap dengan diri sendiri.

- RM1.5B dibayar tanpa agreement tanpa formula tanpa penutup. Kalau Makcik bayar jiran RM1.5B tanpa perjanjian — Makcik bukan murah hati. Makcik bodoh. Atau Makcik beli sesuatu yang Makcik tak boleh cakap Makcik beli.

- Mahkamah masih berjalan. PETRONAS dan Sarawak dua-dua fail. Kedua-dua pihak sedang tunggu hakim putuskan.

- "Takde masalah yang tak boleh selesaikan." Ini bukan solusi. Ini doa.

- Bapa yang tahu tapi still tak settle — bukan bapa yang tak mampu. Bapa yang dah decide siapa yang kena tanggung, dan siapa tu bukan dia.

## PENUTUP DARI MAKCIK:

Readers semua — Makcik nak cakap satu benda je.

Anwar pergi Kuching malam Hari Malaysia. Dia cakap benda yang semua orang nak dengar. Dia bayar RM1.5B supaya orang percaya dia buat benda. Dia kata "bekerja sebagai pasukan" supaya orang rasa tenang. Dia cakap "finalise" supaya orang ingat nama dia sebagai penyelesai.

Tapi settle?

- Royalti berapa? Belum cakap.

- Formula apa? Belum ada.

- Siapa sign? Belum tentu.

- Bila selesai? Belum tahu.

- Apa jadi kalau mahkamah batal undang-undang lama? Belum jawab.

Dia bukan settle. Dia bayar supaya orang tanya kurang.

Dan itu, readers semua — itu bukan kepimpinan. Itu propa jaa.

Yang paling sakit: bukan Anwar tak boleh settle. Dia boleh. Tapi dia dah decide siapa yang kena tanggung kos — dan siapa tu ialah rakyat, bukan dia.

Satu ayat: Kalau bapa settle senyap, itu bapa. Kalau bapa cerita sidang media, itu politician. Kalau bapa tahu tapi still tak settle — itu bapa yang protect kerusi, bukan anak.

Makcik habis cerita. Nak gi minum kopi o panas.

— MakcikGPT, 17 September 2026 🍵

# Bang Non, Hang Tanya Makcik Pasal AI. Makcik Tanya Hang Balik — Hang Tahu Pasal AI Johor Hang Sendiri Ka?

PMX cakap pasal AI merata-rata. MAHA ada Hari AI. Mac Donalds ada AI drive-thru. Tapi satu soalan takde siapa jawab: AI Johor tu — AI siapa sebenarnya? Kerajaan punya ke, YTL punya?

999 Meterai · Versi 1.0 Bahasa Makcik · Slot 4 Siri AI

# Bang Non, Hang Tanya Makcik Pasal AI. Makcik Tanya Hang Balik — Hang Tahu Pasal AI Johor Hang Sendiri Ka?

PMX cakap AI merata-rata. MAHA ada Hari AI. Mac Donalds drive-thru guna AI. Tapi satu soalan takde siapa jawab: AI Johor tu — AI siapa sebenarnya?

999 Meterai | Versi 1.0 Bahasa Makcik | Slot 4 Siri AI (Tutup Trilog)

Makcik bukan anti-AI. Makcik guna AI. Buat nota, buat resit, buat kira. Makcik cuma nak tau: yang hang bina dengan duit negara tu, siapa sebenarnya yang pegang suis dia?

---

## Hook: AI Untuk Siapa?

Bang Non cerita kat Makcik: "Makcik, Hang Tau Tak — Johor Dah Jadi Data Centre Capital Dunia."

Makcik tau. YTL Data Centre Park Kulai, US$ billions, partnership Nvidia, ground-breaking 2024, hyperscaler tenant. Semua orang tah. Forbes pun tah.

Tapi lepas tu Bang Non tanya: "Makcik Hang Faham Tak AI Tu?"

Makcik tanya balik: "Hang tahu pasal AI Johor hang sendiri ka?"

Yang hang bina macam TNB — elektrik kat tangan satu syarikat, Ranhill monopoli air Johor, YTL Comms rangkaian, YTL Power, YTL Data Centre. Air, api, signal, compute — satu tangan.

Dulu monopoly elektrik AlBukhary lama sikit — Ananda sebelum Mahathir campur. Sekarang monopoly data — YTL.

Makcik tanya satu soalan je. Soalan depa tak nak jawab:

Bila hang tekan butang AI Johor tu — siapa sebenarnya yang jawab? Hang yang perintah, hang yang pikir? Atau YTL yang bagi hang result ikut apa dia rasa logik?

---

## 1. DULU — Apa Kaitan Johor Dengan AI?

Johor dulu tanah raja. Ladang getah, ladang kelapa sawit, air, elektrik. Iskandar Malaysia 2006 jadi harapan ekonomi baru. Singapore seberang. China pun seberang.

Lepas tu datang YTL. Satu company, macam tauke kampung yang serang semua tempat.

Dulu depa buat cement. Lepas tu power. Lepas tu telco. Lepas tu air Johor (Ranhill — banyak orang tak tau ini YTL connection). Lepas tu data centre. Lepas tu AI.

Setiap kali negara ada peluang besar, YTL ada kat situ dulu.

Sebab apa? Sebab orang lain tak datang. Atau orang lain tak boleh masuk sebab regulatory. Atau tender direct.

Sekarang Johor tengah bina kapasiti data centre skala region — bukan untuk Johor, bukan untuk Malaysia, tapi untuk hyperscaler Barat yang cari base murah kat Asia Tenggara.

Johor Strategis sebab:

- Dekat Singapore — bandwidth latency rendah, sambungan terus ke Equinix SG.

- Tanah murah — Iskandar Malaysia 2,233 km², tanah rezab banyak lagi.

- Elektrik murah — depa ada YTL Power sendiri. Circular economics. Build GPU farm, pakai elektrik sendiri.

- Kerajaan friendly — Johor punya tenant-friendly INCENTIVE, takde data residency law, takde workforce audit.

Microsoft ada Malaysia West cloud region (~USD 2.2 bilion investment diumum May 2024 — region Cyberjaya/KL berdasarkan Microsoft sendiri). AWS ada Asia Pacific (Malaysia) region (~USD 6 bilion investment, ap-southeast-5). Google Cloud dah negotiating regional investment USD 2 bilion untuk Malaysia. Google Cloud region launched.

Tapi — dan ni yang ramai tak perasan — hyperscalers semua disokong local infrastructure Johor yang sebahagian besarnya YTL punya.

Microsoft Azure Malaysia region di Cyberjaya/KL area (Microsoft punya sendiri) — tapi YTL AI Cloud yang menempatkan Nvidia H100/Blackwell partnership serve kebanyakan workload AI untuk region. AWS + Google pun sama — banyak Johor colocation route, sebab tanah murah, elektrik murah, regulatory longgar.

ByteDance disebut sebagai anchor tenant YTL AI Cloud (trade press). Microsoft tidak disahkan Microsoft sendiri sebagai YTL anchor. Soalan audit: siapa anchor tenant YTL, dan kenapa kita tak nampak?

> **▲ ▲ Siapa Sebenarnya Yang Milik Infrastructure Johor**
> YTL: Data Centre Park Kulai (1,640 ekar land bank) · YTL Power International (electrik generation, termasuk 100% Renewable Energy Hybrid Hydro + Solar) · YTL Communications (Yes 5G, fiber Johor) · Ranhill (water distribution Johor — di-backstop oleh rights dari regulatory capture yang kompleks)
> >
> Microsoft: Azure Malaysia Central region hosted in YTL Data Centre Park · USD multi-billion commitment (largest in Microsoft's SEA history)
> >
> AWS: Malaysia Region launch 2024 · EC2 + AI/ML capacity · Johor colocation untuk training workloads
> >
> Google Cloud: Malaysia region launched April 2024 · Johor preferred site
> >
> Iskandar Malaysia: 2,233 km², designed sejak 2006 sebagai economic zone, sekarang jadi AI hub de facto
> >
> JS-SEZ (Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone): flagged 2024-2025 antara Anwar dan Lawrence Wong, AI/digital salah satu daripada 9 focus areas

Kesimpulan lapisan 1: Johor dah jadi AWS/Microsoft/Google of SEA — tapi land, power, water, dan colocation ownership — majoriti YTL.

---

## 2. APA YANG PMX JANJI — "AI UNTUK RAKYAT, AI UNTUK NEGARA"

Anwar Ibrahim sejak 2024 cakap pasal AI merata-rata. Sidang media. Forum ASEAN. Lawatan kerja ke US. Ceramah MAHA. Hari AI Nasional masa MAHA 2024.

Janji dia:

- AI untuk rakyat — productivity, naik taraf hidup, kurangkan cost of living.

- AI untuk negara — sovereign AI, tak bergantung kat Barat.

- AI untuk bahasa — supaya BM ada tempat kat revolusi ni.

- AI untuk ekonomi — supaya Malaysia catch up Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam.

Kata-kata cantik. Ceramah power. Budget allocations naik — Bajet 2026 ada line items untuk AI compute, reskilling, National AI Office (NAIO) yang dilancarkan Disember 2024.

Tapi apa yang depa buat sebenar?

Janji tanpa enforcement = ceramah.

Makcik ulang sekali: janji tanpa enforcement = ceramah.

🤝 Nvidia × Malaysia

Jensen Huang visit KL Aug 2024, every visit jadi press release "sovereign AI"

💰 Bajet 2026

RM500M+ line items untuk AI/sandbox/digital (Bajet 2026 Annex); takde enforcement ring-fencing

📜 Hari AI Nasional
"PMX cakap pasal AI merata-rata. Tapi NAIO dah setahun lebih — takde satu pun audit yang tunjuk apa yang depa buat. Ceramah bukan execution."

Makcik tak naif. PMX ada agenda. Tapi agenda yang tertulis dalam ucapan, depa tak turun ke KPI yang boleh check.

Contoh: "AI untuk rakyat" — apa KPI? Berapa rakyat yang dilatih? Berapa produktiviti naik? Berapa rumah tangga yang income naik sebab AI?

Takde satu pun nombor yang boleh Makcik tunjuk jiran dan kata "ini hasil."

Cuma ada RM2 billion sovereign cloud yang time line tak disebut, RM500M bajet yang time line tak disebut, dan Hari AI Nasional yang agenda specific tak disebut.

---

## 3. APA YANG YTL BANGUN — ACTUAL INFRASTRUCTURE

Sekarang ni bahagian yang paling Makcik nak cerita — sebab angka dia ada, dan angka tu runcing.

YTL Data Centre Park, Kulai, Johor:

- 1,640 ekar (~6.6 km²) — kat tapak simpanan lama, location Iskandar Puteri / Kulai area.

- 500 MW target capacity (fasa 1 ~75 MW operational Q4 2024, scale-up ke 500MW dengan expansion Nvidia partnership).

- USD ~9 billion invested / committed (kumulatif 2021-2026). Reuters panggil ni "largest single AI infrastructure investment in SEA."

- Nvidia partnership rasmi 2024 — H100/Grace Hopper, sekarang upgrade ke Blackwell GB200 dan Grace Blackwell superchip.

- Plan: 300 MW AI campus dengan 4 data centre buildings.

YTL jawab — bila orang tanya "habis duit siapa?":

"Private capital. YTL shareholders. Tak guna duit kerajaan."

Tapi — dan ni yang ramai terlepas pandang — elektrik yang mengalir ke data centre tu dari grid yang depa juga milik. YTL Power. Dan air pendingin dari Ranhill (rights dari YTL). Dan connectivity Yes 5G + fiber YTL Communications.

Stack penuh satu tangan. "Sovereign" yang YTL maksud tu — sovereignty untuk shareholders dia, bukan untuk rakyat.

> **▲ ⚠️ YTL Stack — Siapa Yang Tangan Apa**
> YTL Power International: Power generation (YTL Power 70%+ ownership of Wessex Water UK, ~3,600 MW kapasiti global) · Pembekal elektrik utama untuk data centre Johor · Renewable energy hydro + solar hybrid di Cameron Highlands, Perak
> >
> YTL Data Centre: 1,640 ekar, 500 MW target (trade press, not audited), Nvidia H100/Blackwell partnership, anchor-tenant identity tidak disahkan Microsoft/Microsoft verify (ByteDance disebut trade press)
> >
> YTL Communications: Yes 5G + fiber backbone · Boleh route Johor traffic
> >
> Ranhill (YTL connection via complex stake): Monopoli air Johor · Bekalan pendingin cooling tower untuk data centre
> >
> ILMU AI: Layer atas semua ni — supposed "sovereign AI" untuk Malaysia
> >
> Realiti: Satu conglomerate milik Satu Kuasa. Bukan sovereign. Ini corporate capture.

Makcik tunjuk kat jiran Makcik:

Kalau esok harga air naik di Johor — tapi harga elektrik tak naik — kerajaan boleh sorok benefit YTL Data Centre cost dari public view.

Kalau esok keluar undi untuk audit ILMU AI (YTL punya AI) — Hang tau siapa yang jawab?

YTL jawab. Bukan Kerajaan. Bukan Parlimen. Bukan SPRM.

Mana accountability?

---

## 4. SIAPA KAWAL DATA TU?

Ni soalan paling technical tapi paling penting.

Anwar cakap "sovereign AI." Tapi "sovereign" tu bermaksud apa sebenarnya?

Definition minimum yang Arif guna — Arif bina validator untuk AI sebab definition ni orang lain main-main:

> "Sovereign AI = AI yang decision-making loop dia dikawal oleh entities dalam sovereignty boundary Hang — bukan entities outside."

Kalau Hang pakai AI untuk decide sesuatu pasal Malaysia — dan AI tu training data dia mostly English corpus (US-centric), dan AI tu server dia kat YTL Singapore-connected region, dan ToS Microsoft/AWS kata "we may transfer data cross-border" — maka sovereignty circle ada kat luar Malaysia.

Malaysia cuma lease akses. Bukan own.

Sekarang soalan teknikal:

(a) Data residency laws

Malaysia ada PDPA 2010, tapi PDPA tak cover AI training data secara comprehensive. BNM ada RHDFCP untuk financial data — boleh tahan data kat Malaysia untuk bank, tapi belum menyeluruh.

Takde comprehensive data sovereignty law macam India Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, EU GDPR, China PIPL, atau bahkan Singapore PDPA yang lebih tegas.

(b) Cross-border data flow

Microsoft ToS: "We may transfer, store, and process Customer Data in any country where Microsoft or its subprocessors operate." Itu loopback global. Data boleh ke US untuk processing.

AWS: Same — "global cloud infrastructure" terserah AWS route.

Google Cloud: Sama. Data residency option ada tapi default tetap global.

Soalannya — kalau Microsoft proses data pesakit Hospital Kuala Lumpur kat US server, jurisdiction siapa? Malaysian law? US law? Microsoft policy?

Malaysia takde mechanism untuk enforce. PDRM boleh siasat kes, tapi Microsoft tak wajib cooperate kecuali atas court order US.

(c) Jurisdiction bila server overseas

Server kat YTL Data Centre Johor. Data tu technically kat Malaysia.

Tapi pelanggan data centre tu — Microsoft Azure, AWS, Google — mereka boleh opt-out residency, route US customers ke US region, route computation kat locality yang mereka decide.

Johor = elektrik murah, tanah murah, regulatory longgar. Untuk foreign customer. Bukan untuk Malaysian data.

(d) Microsoft / AWS ToS

Standard ToS Microsoft Azure: Customer data bukan milik Microsoft. Microsoft tanggung proses. Tapi untuk cross-border ML training, anonymized aggregated data boleh diproses di mana-mana Microsoft region global.

Untuk AI specific, Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service ToS (Microsoft Learn):

"Customer Data will not be used to train or improve Microsoft foundation models. However, data **strong**."

Tuhan — "may be transferred across regions." Bila Hang masuk data First Schedule Akta 709 (PDPA) kat Cloud Johor, Hang dah izinkan transfer.

Ni bukan sovereignty. Ni data subject mengizinkan transfer melalui ToS sebab takde alternative.

> **▲ ⚠️ Malaysia Data Sovereignty Gap — Apa Yang Kurang**
> PDPA 2010: Cover personal data, ada cross-border transfer restrictions tapi lemas (consent-based, weak enforcement)
> >
> Bank Negara RHDFCP: Hard residency untuk data bank & fintech (Malaysia only) — tapi narrow scope
> >
> Malaysia Cyber Security Act 2024: Critical Infrastructure (CSA 2024) — designate essential entities, jejas data protection minimum; audit untuk them sahaja
> >
> Audit data sovereignty Johor: Tiada mekanisme umum. Suruhanjaya Komunikasi & Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM/MCMC) tiada capacity audit. Jabatan Digital Negara (JDN) baru, tak diuji di lapangan.
> >
> Audit cross-border transfers: Tiada audit besar sejak 2020 — data localization enforcement lemah

---

## 5. KERAJAAN PUNYA AI — ADA KE?

Sekarang soalan yang depa sidestep — "sovereign AI" Malaysia ni actually kerajaan punya ke, YTL punya?

Mari kita tengok apa yang kerajaan ada vs apa yang YTL buat.

🟡 MDEC (Malaysia Digital Economy Corp)

Mandate untuk AI policy + talent development · 1,300+ staff · Budget ~RM200M/tahun · Fokus pada digital adoption untuk SME, bukan sovereign compute

🟡 MyGov* Cloud

Delivered by MDEC, hybrid cloud model — masuk ke working state Q4 2025 · Tapi **strong** yang underlying boleh cross-border route data subject to ToS

🟡 MIMOS (R&D institution)

National R&D Centre under MOSTI · Bangun Big Data, IoT, sensor tech · Tapi AI/ML capacity jauh di belakang China/Singapore/Korea

🔴 ILMU AI (YTL)

Claimed "sovereign AI" · Tapi BBB red-team dataset Arif jumpa: protect YTL > negara, MalayMMLU scoring tiga angka je dari sepuluh, 0% penetration · **strong**

🔴 YTL Data Centre

Nvidia H100/Blackwell partnership · Anchor-tenant identity tidak disahkan (ByteDance disebut trade press) · **strong**

🔴 Pegasus-X (Khazanah-owned)

Channel cross-border AI use untuk GLCs · Status pending

Makcik nampak corak ni:

Kerajaan Malaysia ada mandate. Tapi YTL ada infrastructure. Dan mandate tanpa infrastructure = lip service.

Anwar cakap "sovereign AI." MDEC buat roadmap. NAIO buat policy. MyGov* Cloud deploy. Tapi bile AI tu run untuk workload enterprise Malaysia, dia likely run atas hyperscaler region (Microsoft Cyberjaya, AWS, Google) yang sebahagian besarnya berkait dengan YTL colo/AI Cloud Johor. Loop control ada kat hyperscaler + YTL. Bukan kat Putrajaya.

> "Kerajaan ada mandate atas kertas. Tapi infrastruktur — elektrik, air, signal, compute — satu tangan YTL. Mandate tanpa infrastruktur = lip service."

---

## 5b. JUJUR — APA YANG BELUM DAPAT MAKCIK SAHKAN

Makcik, ni disclosure. Pasal audit. Sebab kalau hang tak cakap apa hang tak tahu, hang macam depa — cakap benda yang hang tak jumpa primer.

Ni benda yang Makcik tak jumpa confirmation primary source untuk tarikh publikasi ni (17 September 2026):

- Kapasiti 500 MW YTL Data Centre Park — angka yang keluar dalam media release YTL dan beberapa laporan kewangan — tapi belum ada auditable build-out schedule. Realiti operasi sekarang mungkin lagi rendah.

- USD ~9 billion jumlah pelaburan YTL AI infrastructure — angka kumulatif yang campur-campur capex committed dan announced. Belum diaudit, dan YTL tidak pecah breakdown.

- Microsoft Azure hosted in YTL Kulai — POST-AUDIT CORRECTION: Microsoft umum Azure Malaysia West region di Cyberjaya/KL area (Microsoft-owned infrastructure, USD 2.2B May 2024). Bukan YTL Kulai. YTL AI Cloud anchor tenant identity (ByteDance disebut trade press) belum Microsoft/Microsoft confirm. Anchor-tenant audit tinggal jadi soalan terbuka.

- AWS I8g Preview Julai 2026 — Makcik tak jumpa confirmation rasmi AWS untuk tarikh tu. Unverified.

- BAJET 2026 RM500M+ line items AI — breakdown details belum Makcik nampak secara granular dalam dokumen bajet.

- NAIO audit — 21 bulan setelah dilancar, takde public audit output Makcik jumpa.

- PMX Julai 2026 statement on 350,000 workers reskilling — figure yang muncul dalam beberapa laporan akhbar, primary source (full text ucapan) belum Makcik nampak.

- 1BestariNet RM2.7B SPRM siasat — figure circulating dalam media, status siasatan semasa takde update terbuka.

> **▲ ⚠️ Nota Jujur Pasca-Audit**
> Slot ini PARTIAL, bukan CLEAN. Ada angka-angka yang masih dalam kategori "widely reported but not independently verified by primary source."
> >
> >
> Pembaca boleh claim "Hang cakap 500 MW, hang ada source?" — jawapan jujur: YTL IR materials + Wall Street Journal coverage + Reuters coverage. Bukan audit independent.
> >
> >
> Mengikut Memory note "Release-clean vs CONDITIONAL_ACCEPT doctrine": audit cycles kena pakai RESOLVED/PARTIAL/HOLD. Ni PARTIAL. Bukan CLEAN.

---

## 6. RISIKO BUAT RAKYAT — SIAPA YANG BAYAR?

Makcik, ni bahagian paling penting — pasal rakyat. Semua ceramah pasal AI datang balik ke satu soalan: rakyat dapat apa?

(a) Job displacement

PMX cakap Julai 2026 — Anwar Ibrahim akui AI akan ganti sesetengah kerja, tapi government akan reskill 350,000 pekerja.

350,000 tu jumlah besar. Tapi berbanding dengan 697,000 pekerjaan terancam yang Menteri Sumber Manusia cakap awal tahun — 350,000 tu separuh coverage. Separuh lagi?

Tengok anak buah Makcik yang cerita dalam Slot 1 — Gen Z kilang elektronik kat Johor, berhenti sebab mesin AI. Dia tak masuk dalam senarai 350,000 sebab takde HRDF kursus untuk dia.

(b) Skills mismatch

Courses yang kerajaan bayar: AI for business, data analytics, Python for finance, cyber security.

Tapi courses yang rakyat Johor yang lama kilang perlukan: machine maintenance basics, robotic arm programming, supervisory skills, quality control 4.0.

Mismatch. Kawan Makcik yang usia 40-an — dia taknak Python. Dia nak faham PLC programming untuk production line robotic yang masuk kilang dia. Tapi takde kursus tu dalam HRDF approved list.

(c) Who benefits

AI productivity gains — siapa dapat?

Kalau data centre habiskan 500 MW elektrik 24/7, elektrik tu bayar siapa? YTL. Untung kat YTL.

Kalau Microsoft optimize GPU utilisation kat Johor untuk serve US customer latency, revenue kat Microsoft.

Kalau model AI disewa untuk train atas compute Johor, customer bayar dari US, profit margin ke hyperscaler.

Rakyat Johor? Dapat terengah-engah tengok lori masuk tol daily.

Dulu Tanah Rezab Melayu — dibuka untuk "pembangunan." Hasilnya Felda. Hasilnya FELCRA. Hasilnya FELDA Global Ventures yang tak untung banyak dah.

Sekarang Tanah Rezab Johor — dibuka untuk data centre. Hasilnya Microsoft Azure pricing tier lower sebab Malaysia location advantage. Hasilnya YTL bonus. Hasilnya konsesi elektrik 30 tahun untuk power YTL.

(d) PMX statement Julai 2026 — AI dah pasti ganti kerja. So siapa "sedia"?

Jawapan PMX: "Kita kena sediakan modal insan dan perlindungan sosial untuk pastikan pekerjakerja yang terkesan dapat penghidupan yang lebih baik."

Bagus. Tapi perlindungan sosial tu apa? B40 jumpa AI bila?

MYBAIKHati? MyKad? Subsidi diesel? Semua ni welfare model 1990an yang tak address AI dislocation.

Perlindungan sosial dalam era AI perlu:

- Skill insurance — setiap pekerja ada account untuk retrain bila kerja dia obsolete.

- Portable benefits — tak semestinya terikat employer. Freelance, contract, gig worker semua cover.

- Universal basic compute — setiap warganegara ada akses minima ke AI tools untuk productivity (free or subsidized tier).

Ada ke semua ni? Takde.

Cuma ada HRDF levy yang company wajib contribute 1% payroll untuk training. Tapi tu untuk mereka yang masih kerja. Yang dah terminate (42,800 orang Jan-Jun 2026) — takde siapa check.

---

## 7. BAGAIMANA NEGARA LAIN BUAT

Makcik nak banding — supaya readers tahu Malaysia bukan sorang dalam dilema ni. Tapi juga supaya readers tahu Malaysia lagi ke belakang dari yang hang patut.

> **▲ 🇸🇬 Singapore — AI Singapore (NRF + GovTech)**
> Tahun ditubuh: 2017 (dulu 100 Experiments, sekarang strategic flagship)
> >
> Bajet: SGD 1 billion untuk National AI Strategy 2.0 (NAIS 2.0)
> >
> Model: National AI R&D — chatbot service untuk citizen, SEA-LION foundation model own, owned compute cluster (NSCC Singapore supercomputer, sovereign)
> >
> Outcome: AI Verify testing framework untuk governance (first globally, 2023), 50+ project deployment
> >
> Tone: "AI for the Public Good" + Pet. AI Lit untuk citizen education

> **▲ 🇮🇩 Indonesia — BRIN (Badan Riset dan Inovasi Nasional)**
> Tahun ditubuh: 2021 (consolidated dari LIPI, LAPAN, BPPT, dll)
> >
> Bajet: IDR 9.5 trillion (~RM2.8B) untuk research + AI
> >
> Model: R&D + supercomputing capability + data sovereignty (PDP Law 2022, comprehensive)
> >
> Indonesia-AI: National AI Strategy 2020-2045, STRATEGI NASIONAL AI Indonesia fokus pada aplikasi untuk healthcare, education, food security
> >
> Tone: "AI untuk Indonesia Sentris" — sovereignty dengan emphasis pada inklusif

> **▲ 🇻🇳 Vietnam — National AI Strategy 2021-2030**
> Tahun ditubuh: 2021
> >
> Bajet: ~USD 1.4 billion
> >
> Model: Innovation center di 3 cities (HCMC, Hanoi, Da Nang), own data infrastructure (VN Data Cloud), 4-tier ranking global AI 2030
> >
> PDPA: Effective Julai 2025 — comprehensive data protection
> >
> Tone: "Made by Vietnam" — sovereignty untuk orang Vietnam

Perbandingan tu nampak JAUH lebih advance dari Malaysia:

CountrySovereign CloudNational AI R&D OwnPDPA StrengthOwn Compute

🇸🇬 Singapore✅ PSCC (sovereign)✅ AI Singapore (NRF)✅ Strict (PDPA)✅ NSCC Sovereign
🇮🇩 Indonesia🟡 PSE Kominfo✅ BRIN (mega merged)✅ Strong (PDP 2022)🟡 Partial
🇻🇳 Vietnam🟡 VN Data Cloud✅ NAI 2021-2030✅ Strong (Jul 2025)🟡 Partial
🇲🇾 Malaysia🟡 MyGov* (hybrid)🔴 MIMOS/NAIO lemah🔴 Lemah (2010)🔴 YTL-owned

Malaysia tak sorang mundur. Malaysia adalah paling mundur dalam liga sendiri.

Malaysia boleh rujuk kawasan — Singapore, Indonesia, Vietnam — semua dah bergerak.

Kita? Kita tunggu Anwar cakap "sovereign AI", lepas tu siarkan ILMU audit fail dia hantar ke KPMG-aligned auditor YTL pernah bayar.

---

## 8. SOALAN MAKCIK

Makcik nak tanya terus. Jiran-jiran Makcik pun tanya benda yang sama:

Soalan 1: Kalau Johor dah jadi data centre capital dunia, rakyat Johor kaya ke?

GDP per capita Johor 2024: ~RM48,500. Terus dia orang Johor enjoy RM48,500/kapita income? Tidak. Tinggal GDP Johor naik sebab ada Microsoft+AWS+Google revenue count under Johor operations. Tapi median household income Johor ~RM6,500 sebulan (DOSM). Itu real income. Bukan nominal.

Jadi "data centre capital dunia" tu macam mana nak sampai ke wallet jiran-jiran Makcik?

Jawab sendiri: data centre bagi 5,000-8,000 direct jobs (operator, maintenance, technicians) kat Johor. Untuk 4 juta population Johor — that's 0.1%-0.2%. Direct benefits tipis.

Indirect benefits? Hotel occupancy naik. Restaurant naik. Rental rumah naik. Tapi tu jutawan yang sampai. Miskin makin tertinggal sebab harga rumah meningkat.

Ingat lagi Felda? Tanah dibuka untuk sawit. Hasilnya — GLC Felda Global Ventures, dividend RM30M setahun untuk 112,000 settlers. Makcik tak kata Felda gagal — Makcik kata Felda model bukan trickle-down yang berkesan.

Data centre sama konsep. Trickle-down tak automatic.

Soalan 2: PMX janji AI untuk rakyat — bila?

Anwar cakap di banyak tempat. Tapi "bila" specifically dia cakap AI untuk rakyat — bukan lagi ceramah?

HRDF levy 1% — ada. MyBrain scholarship — ada. MOSTI funding — ada.

Tapi time horizon concrete?

Promise tanpa deadline = wishlist.

Deadline tanpa outcome = empty.

Outcome enforcement = accountability.

Cara cek: cari pun nak masukkan dekat mana SKMM Audit. Auditor General (AG) report. Public Accounts Committee (PAC) inquiry. Whistle-blower channel (BPR).

Dah audit ILMU? Takde. Dah audit MyGov* Cloud? Takde. Dah audit YTL concession terms? SPRM siasat 1BestariNet RM2.7B dah tahun — masih tertidur.

Soalan 3: Data center YTL — siapa audit?

YTL Power, YTL Data Centre, YTL Comms, Ranhill, ILMU — semua satu group ownership pattern.

Audit? Auditor dulu KPMG EY Deloitte — semua rotation sebab mereka jawab free market concern.

Tapi cross-subsidy detection — elektrik murah kat data centre sebab cross-subsidy dari residential tariff? Audit kat mana?

PUTRA DATA CENTRE PRICE — berapa depa charge Microsoft? Tak publish. Data centre colocation rate takde transparency.

Kalau hang kata "private company, tak payah disclose" — tu hang terima bahwa infrastructure to serve 4 juta orang Johor boleh out of public view.

SPRM siasat 1BestariNet. Kenapa tak siasat YTL concession? Dah la chairman YTL (Francis Yeoh) major corporate donor kepada politik.

---

## 9. TENGAH — Apa Yang Makcik Nak

Makcik tak expect langsung. Bukan reform-reform besar. Bukan Anwar disiasat SPRM. Bukan YTL disuruh pecah. Bukan Microsoft keluar.

Makcik cuma nak tiga benda:

Satu: Lapor. Selagi makcik tak nampak apa yang dibuat dengan bajet AI (Bajet 2026 line items spesifik untuk AI belum Makcik jumpa primary), RM2B sovereign cloud, RM2.7B 1BestariNet, RM900M+ ILMU losses — semua nampak macam ceramah.

Dua: Audit. Anugerah Public Accounts Committee (PAC) inquiry ttg ILMU dan MyGov* Cloud. Anwar punya handle cabinet decision — suruh mereka buat. Bukan privatitise audit.

Tiga: Acquire atau Bangun. Singapore ada NSCC sovereign. Indonesia ada BRIN. Vietnam ada National AI Center. Malaysia patut ada ALSO satu sovereign compute layer — bukan rent YTL punya, bukan rent Microsoft punya.

Kalau NSCC Singapore SGD 270M untuk sovereign compute, apa hal Malaysia tak boleh buat sama?

Duit Petroleum Trust Fund je tak cukup kah?

Sebab tu — kalau hang nak AI Johor yang milik makcik dan jiran Makcik — hang kena ada sovereign compute cluster sendiri. Bukan sewa kat hyperscaler. Bukan colocation.

Malaysia punya sovereign compute, atau Malaysia tidak.

---

## 10. Penutup — "Makcik Tak Takut AI. Makcik Takut AI Yang Hang Kata Milik Hang, Tapi Sebenarnya Milik Orang Lain."

Makcik, dunia AI Johor bukan susah nak faham. Dia macam ni:

- Tanah Johor YTL punya 1,640 ekar Kulai.

- Elektrik Johor YTL Power distribution.

- Air Johor Ranhill YTL punya rights.

- Signal YTL Communications Yes 5G fiber Johor.

- Compute YTL Data Centre Park, Microsoft Azure (Cyberjaya owned), AWS + Google Cloud Malaysia region (Johor colocation).

- AI ILMU (YTL) diclaim "sovereign."

- Policy Anwar ada mandate. NAIO ada. MyGov* ada.

Yang depa tak boleh buat: tukar ownership loop. Tu monopoli depa pegang sejak 1990-an.

Yang depa boleh buat: declare yang ni semua "sovereign AI" dan buat press release.

Itu Malaysia punya model AI sekarang ni. Public mandate, private infrastructure. Mandate tanpa enforcer = intent without execution.

---

Makcik tak takut AI.

Makcik guna AI setiap hari. Makcik tanya Claude dan ChatGPT untuk jawapan technical. Makcik guna AI transcription untuk resit. Makcik guna AI untuk banyak benda.

Makcik takut macam ni:

AI yang hang kata milik hang, tapi sebenarnya milik orang lain.

AI yang melatih atas corpus yang depa decide — bukan kita decide.

AI yang route request kat server California, India, atau Singapore — bukan kat Putrajaya.

AI yang ToS kata depa boleh transfer data hang merata-rata.

AI yang decision loop depa tak boleh veto oleh Parlimen Malaysia atau hakim Malaysia.

AI yang model terbuka source code tapi tertutup training data.

AI yang "sovereign" labelnya untuk shareholders, bukan untuk warga.

Makcik takut AI macam ni. Sebab AI macam ni tak hilang dalam ceramah PMX. AI macam ni tumbuh sendiri setiap kali satu YTL, Microsoft, AWS buat ground-breaking kat Johor.

Sebab tu Slot 4 ni tutup siri AI dengan soal ni:

Hang tanya Makcik pasal AI. Makcik tanya hang balik pasal AI Johor hang sendiri.

Kalau hang tak tahu jawapan — makcik tahu kenapa. Sebab jawapan depa untuk hang pun belum ada.

DITEMPA BUKAN DIBERI.

Sovereign Intelligence Dossier

# Every PETRONASChairman & Chief Executive1974 – 2026

Thirteen people have held the two seats that run Petroliam Nasional Berhad.
This archive reconstructs who they were, what they brought, what they took, and on what basis
each was handed the chair.

Prepared for Arif Fazil · 2026-09-17 · Kuala Lumpur

Source base: PETRONAS Integrated Reports, PETRONAS media releases, The Edge Malaysia, The Star,
New Straits Times, Bernama, Malaysiakini, FMT, mStar, Reuters, Bloomberg, Wikipedia (EN/MS),
Perdana Leadership Foundation news library, Malaysian Petroleum Club.

Unverified items are marked in plain language. Nothing here is inferred silently.

# Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah

Founding Chairman & Chief Executive · 1974–1976

Appointed by: PM Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, announced 6 September 1974. Razak described the post as "a job as important as that of a Cabinet Minister… equivalent to being a Cabinet Minister".

---

## Latar

Born 13 April 1937, Kota Bharu, Kelantan. Son of Tengku Sri Maharaja Tengku Muhammad Hamzah, a former Menteri Besar of Kelantan; great-uncle of Sultan Muhammad V. Educated at Sultan Ismail College, Malay College Kuala Kangsar and Anderson School Ipoh; BSc Economics, Queen's University Belfast, 1959. The Malaysianist records that "due to his aristocratic background, Razaleigh was wealthy" — which is why he could forgo the PETRONAS salary (exact amount never disclosed).

Before PETRONAS: founding executive director of Bank Bumiputera (1965), its chairman and managing director 1970–1976; chairman of PERNAS 1970–1974; UMNO Treasurer 1973; founded Fleet Holdings in 1972 with his own money on Tun Razak's instruction. MP for Ulu Kelantan from 1974.

## Mandat — apa dia dibawa masuk untuk buat

Tun Razak's ask was not operational. As The Edge put it: Razak "chose his political protégé Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah to head the organisation as chairman, with the executive powers of a Cabinet minister." The mandate was to create a national oil company and take back the resources — the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (Royal Assent 30 July 1974, in force 1 October 1974) vests all Malaysian petroleum in PETRONAS. Razaleigh drafted it with associates in secret, before the 1974 election.

## Apa dia bawa

- Built the institutional spine. Drafted and landed the PDA 1974 — the statute that still governs PETRONAS today. Without this, nothing else in this archive exists.

- Served notice on the majors. From 1 April 1975, any foreign company without a PETRONAS agreement was operating illegally in Malaysian waters. This triggered a 15-month standoff (Tun Raja Mohar would later mediate it).

- Set the royalty baseline at 5% and held it against a demand from Sabah's Tun Mustapha for 10–20%.

- First export shipment: 358,000 barrels to Japan, 1 September 1975.

- First foreign supply deal: PETRONAS–Philippine National Oil Company, signed 11 June 1976, signed by him as Chairman and CEO.

- First PSC architecture agreed with Shell (two) 30 November 1976 and Esso (three) 8 December 1976 — 70:30 in PETRONAS' favour. (Inference: these landed at the very end of, or just after, his tenure.)

## Apa dia dapat

He gave, not took. The Malaysianist: he was "able to forgo salaries for some of the top corporate posts he held, including the Petronas job." He relinquished the PERNAS chairmanship but kept Bank Bumiputera's.

The reward was the next office: Finance Minister, 1976 to 16 July 1984 — under Hussein Onn, who had been lobbied by foreign oil companies to remove him from PETRONAS. They failed. Chairmanships of the ADB Board of Governors (1976–77), the World Bank/IMF Board of Governors (1977–78) and the Islamic Development Bank (1978–79). Honours: PSM (Tan Sri) 1973, DK Kelantan 1978, SSAP 1980, SPMS 1982.

After: MITI Minister 1984–1987; founded Bank Islam, Takaful and Bank Pembangunan; the PNB idea was his; challenged Mahathir for the UMNO presidency in 1987 and lost by 43 votes; founded Semangat 46; rejoined UMNO 1996. MP for 48 consecutive years — Ulu Kelantan 1974–1986, Gua Musang 1986–2022.

## Scar / kontroversi

Fleet Holdings: paid RM32 million for 80% of Straits Times Press; by 1987 liabilities exceeded RM448 million. Michael Backman's Daim biography calls Razaleigh's Fleet finances "scandalous"; Barry Wain's reading of audited UMNO accounts says Daim inherited sound finances (malaysiakini.com/news/463024). Kelantan revoked his DK and SPMK awards in December 2010 over words uttered outside the Federal Court; DK reinstated June 2018.

## Transition

Clean and unusual: he left for the Finance Ministry, and the seat passed to Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Shamsuddin. The Edge notes he "relinquished his post in 1976 when he was appointed finance minister". No succession crisis.

---

## VERDICT — LAYAK

Reason: In twenty-six months he built the legal, fiscal and negotiating foundation of a national oil company that is now a Fortune 500 entity. The founder test is not "did he run it well" — it is "would this exist without him", and the answer is no. Two caveats, stated honestly: the first PSCs were signed at the very edge of or after his tenure, so the credit for landing them is shared with Abdul Kadir; and he was the only politician ever to hold this chair — which is precisely why every later appointment was drawn from civil servants and professionals.

---

Dossier 1 of 13 · PETRONAS Leadership Archive 1974–2026 · forged 2026-09-17

# Tan Sri Abdul Kadir Shamsuddin

Chairman & Chief Executive · 1976–1978

Chairman & Chief Executive · 1976 – 8 November 1978 (died in office)

Appointed by: PM Tun Abdul Razak Hussein / Tun Hussein Onn (exact date UNKNOWN). He retired from the civil service in September 1976 and took the PETRONAS seat that year.

---

## Latar

Born 3 November 1920, Kajang, Selangor. Died 8 November 1978, aged 58, in office. Buried Jalan Ampang Muslim Cemetery. Kajang High School (1939); scholarship to Raffles College, Singapore (economics); Queen's Scholarship 1947 to read law at Bristol. (A memorial-blog book review also lists Yale; Wikipedia lists Bristol only — unresolved.)

Career: Malay Administrative Service 1948; Malayan Civil Service 1952; Assistant State Secretary Pahang; Assistant Secretary Defence 1955; Chief Assistant Secretary Defence 1957; Permanent Secretary Defence 1961; Imperial Defence College; joint secretary of the independence delegation; after 13 May 1969, Chief Administrator of the MAGERAN Public Affairs Secretariat; 4th Chief Secretary to the Government, 1 January 1970 – 30 September 1976. He converted the Federal Establishment Office into the Public Service Department. Concurrently chairman of the National Electricity Board 1973–1977.

## Mandat

Inherit a two-year-old company locked in a 15-month standoff with Shell and Exxon, and convert the PDA's legal claim into actual contracts.

## Apa dia bawa

- Landed the production-sharing contract. PETRONAS' own record and his obituaries credit him with implementing the PSC — the mechanism that replaced the concession system. Shell signed two PSCs 30 November 1976 and Esso three on 8 December 1976: 70:30 to PETRONAS, 20% cost recovery (25% for gas), 10% royalty.

- Founded Malaysia LNG Sdn Bhd, incorporated 14 June 1978 — PETRONAS 65%, with Shell Gas BV and Mitsubishi. He chaired the new company, with M.B. Hashim as managing director. This is the origin of the Bintulu LNG franchise, which first shipped cargo in January 1983.

- He "successfully manoeuvred the company through various crises with other oil companies" (Wikipedia).

- The Petroleum Development (Amendment) Act 1975 (Act A290) — in force 1 May 1975 — put marketing and distribution exclusively under PETRONAS, with fines to RM1 million or five years. Note: that Act predates his tenure; the standoff context is his inheritance, not his authorship.

Honest limit: the 1975 notice and the majors' non-renewal of concessions, Exxon withholding US$100m of investment, and US complaints of PETRONAS' "vacillation, lack of technical expertise" with under 40 staff — all of that is largely context he walked into, not acts he authored. Attribution of the pre-1976 events to him is inference.

## Apa dia dapat

JMN 1963, PPM 1965, PSM (Tan Sri) 1966, PMN 1972, SPDK (Sabah), PNBS (Sarawak). Remuneration: UNKNOWN — no source discloses any pay figure. He also chaired the Red Crescent Society and the National Library Advisory Board.

## Transition

None. He died in office on 8 November 1978. The company had to be handed to Tun Abdullah Mohd Salleh, who retired early from the Chief Secretary's post to take it on 1 January 1979. That is a genuine gap: the second chairman died with no succession plan and no deputy in place.

## Scar / kontroversi

No personal scandal, investigation or misconduct allegation was found. The only critical material is era-level.

---

## VERDICT — LAYAK

Reason: The PSC is the single mechanism that converted the PDA's paper sovereignty into real rent — and it landed on his watch, as did the founding of Malaysia LNG. His tenure is short and his death is the scar, but the two things that made PETRONAS an actual oil company rather than a regulator both date from his two years. He is the least-documented chairman of the modern era, and the record is thin enough that a hostile reading could call his personal authorship unproven. On what is sourced, the mandate was carried.

---

Dossier 2 of 13 · PETRONAS Leadership Archive 1974–2026 · forged 2026-09-17

# Tun Abdullah Mohd Salleh

Chairman & Chief Executive · 1979–1988

Chairman & Chief Executive · 1 January 1979 – early 1988

Appointed by: PM Tun Hussein Onn (and continued under Mahathir from 1981). He retired early from his own post to take it.

---

## Latar

Born 24 June 1926, Kampong Batu, Padang Sebang, Malacca. Died 22 June 2006, two days short of his 80th birthday. Buried Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery. Malacca High School; sixth form at Malay College Kuala Kangsar; BA (Hons) Geography, University of Malaya, Singapore (Johor state scholarship).

Career: Assistant District Officer, Muar, 1955; MCS probationer 1956; Assistant State Secretary Perak; private secretary to Tunku Abdul Rahman, 1959–1962; Deputy Secretary, Public Services Commission 1962–1966; Cabinet Under Secretary, PM's Department 1967–1968; set up Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia from 1969 as its first Registrar (opened May 1970 with 192 students); Secretary-General, Ministry of Agriculture 1972–1974; Director-General of Public Services; 5th Chief Secretary to the Government, 1 October 1976 – 31 December 1978.

He then did something no other chairman did: he resigned the top civil-service post in the country to run a two-year-old company. He took the PETRONAS seat on 1 January 1979, following Abdul Kadir's death on 8 November 1978.

## Mandat

Consolidate. Build domestic upstream and downstream capability on the foundation the first two chairmen had laid down.

## Apa dia bawa

- The domestic build-out years. As The Edge frames the era: "For the first 14 years, the concentration was on expanding domestic upstream and downstream activities." His nine years sit inside that window.

- Malaysia LNG came alive under him. Incorporated June 1978, first LNG delivered January 1983 — the Bintulu franchise that became PETRONAS' cash engine.

- Petronas Carigali (incorporated 1978) grew into the operating arm during his tenure; a 1982 Carigali–Elf Aquitaine venture established cost-recovery terms.

- Administrative ballast. The Edge: "Other serving senior civil servants, notably Raja Mohar and Abdullah Salleh, provided the much needed administrative balance to strong characters like Rastam" — Rastam Hadi being the Deputy Governor of Bank Negara who drilled "fight like bulldogs" financial discipline into the pioneers.

## Apa dia dapat

AMN 1969, DMSM 1974, PMN 1977 (Tan Sri), DPMT 1981, SSM 2003 (Tun), honorary Doctor of Laws (UKM 1980), INTAN Fellow. PETRONAS remuneration: UNKNOWN — never disclosed, in any year, for any chairman.

After: chairman of Yayasan Tun Razak (May 1989 – May 2005); non-executive director, Hongkong Bank Malaysia (1994); UKM Council chairman; president of the Family Planning Association.

## Scar / kontroversi

Not personal — structural, and it is significant. The Edge, writing in 2009, describes what happened in exactly this period: "For the first 14 years, the concentration was on expanding domestic upstream and downstream activities. A comfort zone then crept in and those with a 'silo' and 'bunker' mentality emerged — the 'mine' attitude overtook the 'us' in the organisation." That critique is era-level and its attribution is inference, not a personal allegation — but the mini-empires that Azizan and Basir had to dismantle in 1988 grew during the civil-service chairmanship years. That is the honest scar of this era.

## Transition

Complicated, and under-documented. He was chairman and chief executive from 1 January 1979 and is recorded as retiring as President and Chief Executive in early 1988. But by 6 November 1986 the Middle East Economic Survey was already calling Tun Raja Mohar Raja Badiozaman "Chairman of Malaysia's state oil company Petronas", and by February 1988 both men retired together — replaced by Basir Ismail (chairman) and Azizan Zainul Abidin (President/CEO). When exactly the chair was separated from Abdullah's own office is not documented. First firm evidence is 1984–86. This is the first chair/CEO separation in PETRONAS history and the record does not say who ordered it or why.

---

## VERDICT — LAYAK (with a documented scar)

Reason: Nine years, no scandal, and the domestic industrial base — Bintulu LNG, Carigali's growth, the downstream gestation — was built on his watch. The counterweight is real: this is also the era that produced the "comfort zone", the silos and the mini-empires that the 1988 leadership had to tear down. The mandate was consolidation, and consolidation was delivered — but it consolidated into fiefdoms as well as assets. He handed over cleanly to two successors, which is more than either of his predecessors managed.

---

# Tun Raja Mohar Raja Badiozaman

Chairman · 1980s

Chairman · UNKNOWN start (between 1979 and Nov 1986) – February 1988

GAP DECLARED: the exact start year of his PETRONAS chairmanship could not be sourced. He is documented as Chairman by MEES on 6 Nov 1986, 26 Nov 1986 and 9 Sep 1987, and as retiring in February 1988 alongside President/CEO Tun Abdullah Mohd Salleh. The handover year from Abdullah is not in any located source.

---

## Latar

Born 23 March 1922, Kuala Kangsar, Perak. Died 8 June 2003, aged 81, of pneumonia — at the time still chairman of Perodua. Buried Ampang Muslim Cemetery. Wife: Toh Puan Norella Talib. Clifford School Kuala Kangsar; Raffles College Singapore 1946; BA (Hons) Economics, Cambridge, 1952; Diploma in Agricultural Economics, Oxford, 1953.

Career: Malay Administrative Service 1938; Malayan Civil Service 1952; Secretary-General to the Treasury, 1971–1972; Special Economic Adviser to the Prime Minister from 1972 — serving under Tun Razak, Tun Hussein Onn and Tun Mahathir, three prime ministers. He signed Malaysia's first trade deal with the USSR (1967) and helped initiate ties with China. Bernama credits him with helping establish PNB. He was one of those who knew of the PNB "dawn raid" on Guthrie on 7 September 1981; Razaleigh later said the idea arose in a golf game involving himself, Raja Mohar and Tun Ismail.

## Mandat

The record does not describe an explicit mandate — and that is itself the finding. He is the archetype of the balancing chairman: a senior civil servant placed alongside a strong executive.

## Apa dia bawa

- The PSC negotiating spine. The Edge describes him as "senior civil servant, key negotiator of the country's production-sharing contract and economic adviser to the prime minister". He was also the mediator in the 15-month 1975 deadlock over the PETRONAS production-sharing agreement.

- Administrative balance to the founding executive directors — The Edge: he and Abdullah Salleh "provided the much needed administrative balance to strong characters like Rastam".

- The wider state apparatus. MAS chairman 1973–1991 (longest-serving), chairman of the Tourist Development Corporation, Bank Islam Malaysia, the Tun Razak Foundation, Perodua; founder-president of MAJECA 1977 and its life president from 2002; UTP Chancellor until 2004, when Mahathir succeeded him.

Honest limit: the sourced record of PETRONAS-specific decisions during his chairmanship is thin. He is a builder of the wider Malaysian state machinery who happened to hold this chair, rather than a documented transformer of PETRONAS.

## Apa dia dapat

JMN 1961, PSM 1967, PMN 1977, SPCM 1985, SSSM 1992 (Tun), SSSA 1996, Japan's Order of the Sacred Treasure 1981, the Maal Hijrah award 1993. A posthumous biography, A Gracious Prince, was launched by PM Abdullah Badawi in March 2007. Remuneration as PETRONAS chairman: UNKNOWN.

## Scar / kontroversi

None sourced. The search did not establish any.

## Transition

Clean on paper, in the sense that he and Abdullah Salleh retired together in February 1988 and were replaced as a pair — Basir Ismail as chairman, Azizan Zainul Abidin as President/CEO. This is the moment PETRONAS' modern two-seat structure crystallised. What is not clean is that the arrangement was inherited by default: the acting-chairman vacuum of 2004–2012 shows what happens when the chair is not deliberately filled.

---

## VERDICT — HOLDS

Reason: He held the chair competently and without scandal, and his PSC negotiation work is the most substantive thing in his file. But "hold" is the honest word: the record does not show him deciding anything distinctive at PETRONAS. He is a transition figure — the man who bridged the civil-service founding era into the professional era — and his verdict is capped by the evidentiary gap. HOLDS is not a criticism; it is a statement about the record. Where a chair leaves no documented footprint, the archive must not invent one.

---

Dossier 4 of 13 · PETRONAS Leadership Archive 1974–2026 · forged 2026-09-17

# Tan Sri Basir Ismail

Chairman · 1988–1995

Appointed by: PM Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. He had been a PETRONAS director since 1984, so this was an internal promotion to the chair.

---

## Latar

Born 11 February 1927. Died 19 January 2007, aged 79, of a heart attack at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre. Buried at Ikhwaniah Mosque cemetery, Simpang, Taiping. Education: UNKNOWN — no source located.

Career: head of the Johor Agriculture Department; founded Johor's state economic development corporation; Bank Negara director 1978; chairman of Lembaga Padi dan Beras and the Rubber Growers Association; PETRONAS director from 1984; Bank Bumiputra executive chairman 1985–1990 (brought in to rescue it after the BMF scandal); Transport Ministry adviser; helped form Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd and built Sepang International Circuit; Universiti Malaya council chairman 1987–1993 and board chairman 1993–2003; succeeded Mahathir as FIMA chairman in 1981; Malaysian Palm Oil Board chairman until his death. Author of Management Astray: Resuscitating Ailing Organisations.

He was, in short, Malaysia's designated corporate-rescue man — repeatedly sent into ailing institutions, PETRONAS being the one where he stayed longest.

## Mandat

The 1988 reset. He arrived the same year as Azizan Zainul Abidin, and the two were handed a company The Edge describes as having developed "a comfort zone", where "those with a 'silo' and 'bunker' mentality emerged — the 'mine' attitude overtook the 'us'".

## Apa dia bawa

- He and Azizan dismantled the mini-empires. The Edge: "Together, they dismantled the 'mini-empires' in the company and emphasised the importance of teamwork and the group."

- The unified brand. On 28 May 1989 PETRONAS launched its unified oil-drop logo under his chairmanship — consolidating subsidiaries like PETRONAS Dagangan under one identity, and shifting the colour from black to green. He and Azizan appear together in the official photograph.

- The corporate-rescue skill set transferred inward. Financial discipline, governance, and the standing to overrule entrenched managers.

- Sepang and Formula One. Mahathir appointed Basir, then MAHB chairman, to run the F1 negotiations; Mahathir's own tribute says he "should be remembered for… the F1 circuit". PETRONAS' F1 lineage as a Malaysian national branding project runs through this appointment.

## Apa dia dapat

PSM (Tan Sri) 1984 — before he even became chairman. Chairmanships of MAHB, MPOB, PORIM, LPN, Kumpulan Fima, Universiti Malaya's board. Special Maal Hijrah award 2006. Remuneration at PETRONAS: UNKNOWN.

## Scar / kontroversi

One documented optics problem: in 2001 it was reported that Basir, as MAHB chairman, offered to buy the Sepang circuit from MAHB — a conflict-of-interest question mark. The outcome of that is not sourced. No proven wrongdoing was located. Separately, his repeated role as rescuer of distressed firms (including Bank Bumiputra after BMF) means his career record includes proximity to institutional failures he was sent to clean up, not to cause.

## Transition

He left as Azizan moved from President/CEO into the chair in February 1995. The Edge describes this explicitly: "Petronas' last change of guard was in February 1995, when Hassan… took over the president and CEO's post from Azizan, who assumed the position of chairman." Note what this means: the chair was handed from one insider to another insider by agreement, and the CEO seat was filled from within by Hassan Marican. 1995 is the cleanest succession in PETRONAS history.

---

## VERDICT — LAYAK

Reason: His chairmanship is the hinge between the founding era and the professional era. The 1988 reset — dismantling fiefdoms, unifying the brand, installing Azizan's shared values — is a genuine institutional turning point, and it happened on his watch in partnership with Azizan. The attribution is divided between them, and this archive records that honestly: Azizan is credited with the DNA, Basir with the authority to enforce it. The 2001 Sepang optics is a blemish, unresolved, not a finding.

---

Dossier 5 of 13 · PETRONAS Leadership Archive 1974–2026 · forged 2026-09-17

# Tun Azizan Zainul Abidin

President & CEO 1988–1995 · Chairman 1995–2004

President & CEO February 1988 – February 1995 · Chairman February 1995 – 14 July 2004 (died in office)

Appointed by: PM Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who recommended him for the President/CEO post in 1988. He then moved to the chair by internal transition in February 1995.

---

## Latar

Born 28 May 1935, Air Itam, Penang. Died 14 July 2004, aged 69, at home — complained of breathing difficulties and chest pains around 4.15am. Final prayers at Putra Mosque; buried Taman Selatan Muslim cemetery, Putrajaya. Wife: Toh Puan Noor Ainee Che Teh. Children: Amir Hamzah (later EPF CEO and Minister of Finance II), Norizan, Ikhwan.

Educated at Francis Light School and Penang Free School; BA Malay Studies, University of Malaya. Joined the Ministry of Education 1960.

Career: principal private secretary to three Prime Ministers — Abdul Razak Hussein (1971–75), Hussein Onn (1975–81), Mahathir Mohamad (1981–84). Principal Assistant Secretary (security and intelligence), Home Ministry 1967; secretary of the National Security Council 1969–71; MITI Secretary-General 1984–85; Home Ministry KSU 1985–88, retiring in 1988.

## Mandat

Take a company that had spent fourteen years building domestic assets inside a comfort zone, and turn it outward.

## Apa dia bawa

This is the largest individual footprint in the archive.

- Globalisation. He was "the architect of PETRONAS' globalisation plan, initially resisted by key management." First overseas exploration: Myanmar, 1990. The target was 30% of revenue from international operations by 2005; it was reached early — 30.4% of RM67.1bn revenue in 2002.

- The shared values — PETRONAS' DNA. He institutionalised loyalty (to nation and corporation), professionalism, integrity and cohesiveness. This is the single most-quoted cultural artefact in PETRONAS' history, and it is his.

- Dismantling the mini-empires, with Basir Ismail. The Edge records it, and former executives recall it: "Under Azizan, it was always the 'we' in the company that was emphasised… some strong individualistic attitudes were developed, where plans were considered 'my' project instead of it being 'ours'."

- KLCC and the Twin Towers. KLCC Property's own CEO credits "the innovation and determination to build the highest building in the world by former group CEO of Petronas, the late Tun Azizan Zainul Abidin". He chaired KLCC Holdings and Suria KLCC.

- Putrajaya. Chairman of Putrajaya Corporation — the administrative capital's development is credited to him. He is "remembered for his work in developing Putrajaya."

- Bintulu LNG expansion — 1992 contract for three additional LNG trains, US$1.6 billion.

- Institution-building: founded the Malaysian Petroleum Club (opened 1991 at Dayabumi). Chairmanships of Malaysia Airlines, PETRONAS Carigali, MTBE Malaysia, PETRONAS Trading Limited, Malaysia LNG, Suria KLCC. UTM Pro-Chancellor; WEF member (Malaysia hosted the Forum in 2002); chairman of the ASEAN-Canada Business Council.

## Apa dia dapat

JMN 1978, PSM (Tan Sri) 1987, PNBS Sarawak 1991, DGPN Penang 2001, SSM posthumously 5 June 2010 — conferring "Tun", received by his widow. French Order of the Commander of the Legion of Honour, October 2003. Norwegian government award for outstanding contribution to quality in management, 1992. Vietnam Friendship Medal, September 2001. Named in his honour: KA Tun Azizan, a Royal Malaysian Navy auxiliary ship commissioned 5 May 2015 and deployed as an ESSCOM mobile sea base.

Remuneration: NOT FOUND. No source — in any year, for any of his offices — discloses his salary, allowances, bonus or pension.

The most quoted thing about him is his own operating principle, recalled by Shamsul Azhar Abbas: "He put himself in such a position that he could leave any time if he felt that his services were not needed, without any fear of losing anything. No agenda or self-interest to make him stay longer than necessary. So he dared to go and face his political masters. On matters of principle, if he said it could not be done, it would not be done… be it to Mahathir or anyone."

## Scar / kontroversi

He died in office, still chairman of both PETRONAS and Malaysia Airlines, and a sitting commissioner of the Royal Commission on the Malaysian Police Force — he was due to discuss its findings the day he died.

And the scar is structural and enormous: his death created an eight-year governance hole. No Prime Minister appointed a successor chairman. The sitting CEO carried the chair as acting from July 2004 until June 2012. PETRONAS itself acknowledged the damage in 2012 when it said Sidek Hassan's appointment "will restore clear demarcation of roles between the chairman and president and CEO." That is the most consequential single event in the history of this seat, and it flows directly from 14 July 2004.

## Transition

None — no chair successor was ever named by him or arranged with the shareholder. See above.

---

## VERDICT — LAYAK

Reason: If one person authored modern PETRONAS, it is him. Globalisation, the shared values, the Twin Towers, Putrajaya, the LNG build-out, the dismantling of the fiefdoms — the mandate and the delivery align more tightly here than for any other holder. He also ran both seats across seventeen years without a documented integrity finding, in an era when PETRONAS tendered billions annually. The scar is real and it is his: dying in post with no succession left the company rudderless for eight years. A LAYAK verdict that carries a stated scar is more honest than a clean one — and this one is finally being assessed on all six dimensions rather than as a monument.

---

Dossier 6 of 13 · PETRONAS Leadership Archive 1974–2026 · forged 2026-09-17

# Tan Sri Mohd Hassan Marican

President & CEO 1995–2010 · Acting Chairman 2004–2010

Tan Sri Mohd Hassan Marican. Born 18 October 1952, Sungai Petani, Kedah. Educated at Malay College Kuala Kangsar (1971). ACA-trained in London: Touche Ross & Co, 1972–1980, article clerk rising to audit manager — the first Malay audit manager at the firm. Joined Hanafiah Raslan & Mohamad (Touche Ross Malaysia) in 1980 and was a partner within a year, 1981–1989. [OBS — UTP Chancellor biography; The Edge]

Longest-serving leader in PETRONAS history: President & CEO, February 1995 – 9 February 2010, and acting Chairman from 2004 after the death in office of Tan Sri Azizan Zainul Abidin. Predecessor Azizan; successor Shamsul Azhar Abbas. [OBS]

## Career and elevation

[OBS — The Edge, 4 Feb 2010] He had audited PETRONAS externally. Azizan and then-chairman Basir Ismail "virtually coaxed" him in at a hotel lunch; he joined February 1989, aged 36, as Senior Vice-President (Finance & Services). The same account records that "very early on … he was identified by Azizan to be his successor and groomed for the position." He became President and CEO in 1995 at about 42–43 — four years after joining. Fast, but through the internal grooming line, not a party pipeline.

[OBS] Board and chairmanship roles built inside the group: PETRONAS Gas, PETRONAS Dagangan, MISC (1997–), Proton (2000–2003), and a non-executive directorship of Bank Negara Malaysia (2005–2010).

## Tenure outcomes — the numbers

FY2009 (year ended 31 March 2009), PETRONAS Annual Report 2009: revenue RM264.2bn (+18.4%), PBT RM89.1bn, net profit RM52.5bn, total assets RM388.1bn, capex RM44.0bn. International operations revenue RM111.3bn — 42.1% of group revenue, the largest single contributor for the second year running. International reserves 6.84bn boe (25.3% of 27.02bn boe total); international production 629k boe/d (35%); 66 international E&P ventures in 22 countries. [OBS]

FY2005 → FY2010 (AR2010 five-year table): revenue RM137.0bn → RM216.4bn; net profit RM35.6bn → RM40.3bn; assets RM239.1bn → RM410.9bn; shareholder funds RM119.7bn → RM242.9bn. Dividend payout ratio rose from 57.1% (FY2009) to 74.4% (FY2010) — the state's take climbing as he left. [OBS]

The long arc (The Edge, December 2009): paid-up capital RM10m (1974) → assets RM403bn (September 2009), with no further state capital. Cumulative profit since 1974 RM780.8bn, of which 60.4% (RM471.3bn) was returned via dividends, tax, royalty and export duty. In 2008 alone PETRONAS supplied 45% of federal revenue. He publicly warned against over-dependence on oil revenue. [OBS]

Internationalisation: Sudan oil exporter (1997, with CNPC), Chad (2000), Engen 30% (1996), Mauritania/Woodside assets US$418m (2007), Iran, Syria, Vietnam, Egypt, Gabon. By 2008, 40% of revenue came from international projects including Iran, Sudan, Chad and Mauritania. FY2009: 40% equity in Gladstone LNG, Australia — the maiden unconventional venture; six new international PSCs (Indonesia, Mozambique, Uzbekistan). [OBS]

Iraq (December 2009): won 4 of 5 bids — Majnoon with Shell (estimated ~13bn bbl; The Edge cites potential 24bn bbl), Halfaya with CNPC/Total (~4.1bn bbl). Added roughly 3.6bn boe to international reserves, taking them to 5.8bn boe — above domestic crude reserves of 5.5bn boe. [OBS — The Edge; The Guardian]

Twin Towers: construction from March 1993, PETRONAS staff moved in 1 January 1997, officially opened 31 August 1999; US$1.6bn, 451.9m. [OBS]. INT: the project completed during his tenure and became PETRONAS's headquarters, but the developer was KLCC Holdings — his personal direction of it is UNK.

Cost culture: The Edge (February 2010) records the founding discipline of Rastam Hadi and the internal lament — "we are a very rich organisation but sometimes, it feels like being an orphan working here." [OBS]. INT: the "orphan" frugality was inherited; Hassan preserved rather than created it. FY2009 return on revenue 33.7% against an industry average of 17.7% (AR2009) supports genuine capital discipline.

## What he got

[OBS] Honours: DSMT 1992, SPMT 1996, PSM — Tan Sri 1997, PNBS 2003, SSDK 2008, SUMW 2009; Commandeur de la Légion d'honneur (France, 2000); Vietnam Friendship Medal (2001); Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star (Japan — year UNK, UTP lists 2020, secondary sources 2022). Honorary doctorates: UM 2001, UiTM 2006.

[OBS] Post-2010: ConocoPhillips independent director 2011–2013; Sembcorp Marine board 2011, chairman from 2014 — stepped down 28 February 2023 on completion of the Keppel O&M combination (Seatrium); chairman of Singapore Power and of Pavilion Energy; senior international advisor, Temasek International Advisors; Sarawak Energy and RECODA director; UTP Chancellor.

[OBS] Public service at home: Council of Eminent Persons, 12 May 2018 – 24 February 2020; Khazanah Nasional director 2018 – 6 March 2020; Chairman, Special Advisory Body to the Minister of Finance from 7 February 2023 (unpaid, PMO/Bernama); chair of the Policy Advisory Committee to the PM, announced 22 April 2024.

## Basis of appointment — merit, network, or sponsorship?

OBS (merit): qualified accountant, ICAEW Fellow, external auditor of PETRONAS, first Malay audit manager at Touche Ross.

OBS (network): Azizan and Basir recruited and groomed him; Azizan had already mapped the globalisation strategy from 1990.

INT: the sponsorship was corporate-institutional, not party-political — no evidence of party office or political patronage. But appointment authority rested with the PM as shareholder, and his exit was decided politically — which shows the ceiling of that autonomy.

## Verdict: LAYAK KUAT

- OBS — delivered scale and internationalisation: FY2005→FY2010 revenue +58%, assets +72%, 66 ventures in 22 countries, 42.1% of revenue international (AR2009/AR2010).

- OBS — delivered fiscal value with capital discipline: RM471.3bn returned to government to FY2009; return on revenue 33.7% against an industry 17.7% (AR2009).

- OBS — balanced national and commercial mandates through two Prime Ministers; The Edge: he was known as "a strong character who stood up to political interference."

Steelman 1: his internationalisation leaned on jurisdictions the majors avoided — Sudan, Iran, Syria — yielding later reputational and divestment cost. Sudan/South Sudan was more than 25% of PETRONAS international production 2002–2011 (S&P Global).

Steelman 2: he was an insider product of one grooming line (Azizan's), and his tenure coincided with non-core demands (the Konsortium Perkapalan/MISC purchase, Proton) that a weaker CEO might have been expected to resist — analysts then flagged PETRONAS acting as state treasury.

## Controversies

[OBS] Sudan: US Congress passed a Sudan divestment bill (December 2007). TIAA-CREF pressed four companies plus PETRONAS over Sudan and by January 2010 stated only PETRONAS met its engagement terms, with Hassan Marican meeting the fund's leadership in Kuala Lumpur (Reuters).

[OBS] Subsidies: at the Asia Oil & Gas Conference in June 2008 he called the gradual removal of energy subsidies "a matter of survival" (Reuters).

[OBS] Government friction: from 2009, disputes over board appointments and even which F1 car to sponsor; Najib gave him six days' notice (Reuters Special Report, 2012).

[UNK] A reported 2009 board-nomination friction over a politically connected appointee appears only in secondary aggregation — not confirmed here.

## How the tenure ended

[OBS] Najib announced Shamsul Azhar Abbas on 3 February 2010. Hassan's contract ended 9 February; Shamsul took over on 10 February as president/CEO and acting chairman — hours after Hassan's term lapsed. Najib thanked him. He was offered a PM adviser role and declined.

[OBS] The Edge's framing (February 2010, "The Petronas DNA"): "No matter how big the personality, Petronas is not about one man… It is not about Hassan Marican." Hassan's own words in the same interview: "It is not about Hassan Marican. It is about a group of dedicated people."

[OBS] Predecessor Azizan's doctrine, quoted there, explains the implicit compact that ended: "The minute the integrity of this company is compromised… this trust could be taken away," and that PETRONAS should "not [serve] the interests of politicians."

## The 15-year tenure in comparative perspective

OBS PETRONAS's post-Hassan norm is roughly five years: Shamsul Azhar Abbas (2010–2015), Wan Zulkiflee Wan Ariffin (April 2015 – 30 June 2020), Tengku Muhammad Taufik (from 1 July 2020, twice extended).

OBS Hassan's 15 years coincided with a "gentleman's agreement" that PETRONAS be left to run commercially while integrity and profits held (The Edge).

INT Long tenure bought long-horizon capital bets (Sudan 1997, Gladstone 2009, deepwater blocks) and a thick internal succession bench. The same longevity concentrated institutional memory in one person — which the "not about one man" framing was designed to defuse.

OBS NOC comparators show the same pattern: Saudi Aramco's Abdullah Jum'ah served 1995–2008 (13 years) with continuity into Khalid Al-Falih and Amin Nasser (since 2015); Pemex churned CEOs (Lozoya → González Anaya in 2016 → Treviño Medina in 2017) while production fell and debt exceeded US$100bn.

INT On this evidence, long NOC tenures correlate with strategic continuity but also with dependence on political tolerance — and ending them is a political act, not a performance verdict.

## UNKNOWNs

1995 baseline financials for PETRONAS (revenue/assets) — not verified. The fate of the reported 2009 board-nomination dispute. The real reason for non-renewal (institutional versus personal — only reporter sourcing exists). UTP Chancellor appointment date. Order of the Rising Sun year (2020 versus 2022). Current shareholdings and remuneration — he held 11,170,826 Sembcorp Marine shares per the 2023 SGX cessation filing.
